sections.h2: What is the first thing to know about selling a house in Westland?
sections.html:
Before anything else, a Westland seller needs a Certificate of Approval from the city. Every house that is sold or transferred must have one before the residential sale closes, so the certificate sets the pace for the whole deal. The Building Division handles it, and the seller normally opens the file.

Westland is in Wayne County, roughly 18 miles west of downtown Detroit. Deeds for Westland houses go to the Wayne County Register of Deeds, whose appointment system, fees and tax-certification step differ from those in Macomb or Kent counties.

sections.h2: How did Westland grow into the city it is now?
sections.html:
Nankin Township covered this ground until May 16, 1966, when its voters chose to form the City of Westland. The township had reached about 70,000 residents by 1960, the biggest township in Michigan. The vote came after Livonia tried to annex the site of the Westland Shopping Center, which opened in 1965.

Norwayne, one of the oldest subdivisions, was built right after World War II as temporary housing for veterans working in nearby factories. Westland now spans 20.4 square miles, and every census since 1970 has counted between roughly 84,000 and 87,000 residents.

Ford Road (M-153) crosses central Westland. Wayne County's Hines Park lies along the northern edge, and the city maintains its own neighborhood parks. Garbage goes out weekly in the black bin, and the blue recycling bin is picked up every second week.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Westland addresses?
sections.html:
The Wayne-Westland Community School District covers most of the city. John Glenn High School serves central Westland and part of the north, and some southern blocks feed Wayne Memorial High School in the city of Wayne. The far northern edge belongs to Livonia Public Schools, whose Churchill and Franklin high schools take those students.

Corners of southeastern Westland are divided between Romulus Community Schools and the Taylor School District, after the Inkster district was dissolved. Assignments can change within a block, so ask the district about the exact address and pass the answer to the buyer.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Westland homeowners?
sections.html:
Census estimates put Westland at 82,333 people on July 1, 2025, which is 3.6 percent less than the 2020 base of 85,409. The 2020 count found 39,633 housing units, 4.9 percent of them empty. Between 2020 and 2024 the bureau tallied 35,932 households with 2.30 people apiece.

Owners live in only 61.3 percent of Westland homes, a smaller share than in many Michigan suburbs, which is one reason the city's rental rules draw attention. Homes lived in by their owners have a median value of $184,600. Renters pay $1,158 a month at the median, and household income has a median of $62,076. Owners with a mortgage pay $1,360 a month at the median.

sections.h2: How does Westland's Certificate of Approval work?
sections.html:
The seller sends the Building Division (36300 Warren Road, phone 734-467-3210, open weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.) a Home Sale or Transfer application. An inspector then walks the house against the property maintenance code. Inspections can be booked online, by email to building@cityofwestland.com, by phone or at the counter.

  • A mechanical contractor registered with Westland tests the furnace or boiler and signs the city's own certification form.
  • If the home has a fireplace, a chimney contractor files a safety inspection report as well.
  • A seller who completes the process receives a certificate that stays valid for six months.
  • A seller who stops short leaves a second path: the buyer pays $80 for an Approval Letter to Close, files a Remaining Violations Disclosure Form along with the signed purchase agreement, and then gets ninety days to fix the items and book the final inspection.

That second path can suit an as-is cash purchase, because the closing proceeds with the open items and the repairs shift to the buyer.

sections.h2: Do open permits or rentals complicate a Westland sale?
sections.html:
They can. The Building Division issues the permits that homeowners most often skip: re-roofing, decks, fences, fireplaces, garages, pools, kitchen expansions and basement finishing all need one, and electrical, plumbing and heating work each take a separate trade permit. A housing inspector walking the house for the Certificate of Approval is likely to ask about any of that work, so gather permit numbers and final approvals before the visit.

Westland also runs a rental program, with a Rental Registration Application on the Building Division's forms list. An owner selling a tenant-occupied house should ask the Building Division at 734-467-3210 how the registration and the sale certificate interact, and whether the rental registration is current before the house goes under contract.

Westland's Planning and Building Department also lists a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy request form, a separate route used while work is still unfinished. Ask the department whether that form applies to your situation before you promise a buyer a closing date.

sections.h2: What does a Westland sale cost in city and county charges?
sections.html:
The city's fee varies with building type. On the county side, recording a deed costs $26 plus a $4 state survey fee. The county says its schedule of January 1, 2026 was its first increase since 1996. Deeds and land contracts also need Wayne County treasurer certification unless an exemption applies.

Westland sale charges. Sources: City of Westland Home Sale or Transfer application and Wayne County Register of Deeds.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed with the Wayne County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Wayne County has served customers by appointment only since October 1, 2025. A visitor with up to five documents gets a 20 minute slot, while the 45 minute slots go to people filing five to 25. Book on 313-224-5860, or call 313-224-5851 with recording questions.

The county's list of common rejections includes:

  • A photocopied signature where an original is needed.
  • A deed that names neither a consideration amount nor an exemption statute.
  • A first page lacking the 2.5 inch top margin, or type below 10 point.
  • Social Security digits left visible.
  • A warranty deed without the county treasurer's certification.

Transfer tax is accepted as cash, check or money order. Cards work for other charges with matching ID, but American Express and Discover do not. A check more than $25 over the amount due is returned unprocessed.

faqs.q: Is there any way to close a Westland sale without the seller finishing the city inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer pays $80 for an Approval Letter to Close and signs the violations disclosure form with the purchase agreement. That opens a ninety-day period to complete repairs and pass the final inspection.

faqs.q: What fee does Westland charge on a Home Sale or Transfer application?
faqs.a: The rate is $250 for single-family houses, $475 for duplexes and $900 for multi-family buildings, according to the city's application dated Rev. 7-1-26. The seller files it with the Building Division.

faqs.q: How long is a Westland Certificate of Approval valid?
faqs.a: Six months from issue, for a seller who completes the inspection. The city's furnace or boiler certification must be on file before final approval is granted.

faqs.q: Who pays Michigan transfer tax when a Westland house sells?
faqs.a: The seller. Wayne County lists $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, collected as the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does Wayne County require an appointment to record a Westland deed?
faqs.a: Yes, since October 1, 2025. Daily slots start at 8:00 a.m. and the last begins at 3:50 p.m. For property tax amounts and due dates, ask the Westland Finance Department before closing.
